problem: Determine the largest union of intervals on which the function $f(x)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2x+4}$ is continuous.

feedback.problem: Determine the largest union of intervals on which the function $f(x)=\frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-4x+3}$ is continuous.
feedback.worked_solution:
This is a rational function, so it is continuous at all points in its domain. To find its domain, we start by factoring the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-4x+3} \\  & =\frac{x-1}{(x-1)(x-3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-3},\end{aligned}
$$

 

where $x\ne 1.$

This function is continuous everywhere except at the excluded points $x=1$ and $x=3.$

Therefore, the domain consists of the union of the intervals $(-\infty ,1),$ $(1,3),$ and $(3,\infty ),$ namely

$$
(-\infty ,1)\cup (1,3)\cup (3,\infty )
$$

and the function is also continuous on this union of intervals.
